sentences.text:
on 15
July, 2024
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice K.Surender
 Criminal Revision Case No.284 of 2010
Order:

This Criminal Revision Case is filed against the Judgment dated 10.02.2010 in Criminal Appeal No.154 of 2008 on the file of the Judge, Family Court, Nalgonda, whereunder the sentence of conviction imposed against the petitioner/accused No.1 in C.C.No.158 of 2007 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate, Nakrekal, was confirmed.

2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner as well as learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent-State and perused the record.
3.
The revision petitioner is the husband, who was convicted by both the Courts below for the offence under Section 498A of IPC and sentenced to undergo one year simple imprisonment.
4. According to the prosecution case, the petitioner was arrayed as accused No.1.
His marriage was performed with PW.1 in the year 1994 and at the time of marriage, Rs.40,000/- cash and two tulas of gold were given as dowry.
Female child was born and thereafter the petitioner and his family members started harassing PW.1 for the reason of giving birth to a female child.
Further, they demanded for a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards additional dowry to clear debts of the petitioner.
The matter was placed before the elders, who asked the petitioner and others to look after PW.1 properly and also paid an amount of Rs.30,000/-.
The petitioner and his family members again started demanding additional dowry of Rs.20,000/-.
The petitioner developed intimacy with accused No.5 and also married her.
The said issue was again taken up by the elders.
However, there was no consensus as such the complaint was filed.
5. Police having investigated into the case, filed charge sheet under Sections 498A and 494 of IPC against the petitioner and others.
Accused No.5 is the alleged woman with whom the petitioner was having illicit relation.

6. Learned trial Court having recorded the evidence of the witnesses viz., PWs.1 to 7 found favour with the version that the petitioner was harassing PW.1, however accused Nos.2 to 7 were acquitted of all the charges.
7. In appeal, the learned Sessions Judge confirmed the conviction recorded by the trial Court against the petitioner/accused No.1 for the offence under Section 498A of IPC.
8. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the Courts below had already acquitted the petitioner for offence under Section 494 of IPC.

Both the offences under Sections 498A and 494 of Vanguri Veeraiah, vs The State Of Ap Rep By Its Pp Hyd., on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155801310/
1 IPC go together.

sentences.text:
In fact, when the trial Court has acquitted the petitioner for the offence under Section 494 of IPC, then question of conviction under Section 498A of IPC does not arise since there are no other specific allegations by PW.1 against the petitioner, but having illegal contact with accused No.5.
9.
The witnesses have clearly narrated regarding the two panchayats that was held and that the petitioner had undertaken to take care of PW.1.
The allegation regarding beating and demand of additional dowry of Rs.30,000/- and again for Rs.20,000/- is consistent.

10. Learned counsel for the petitioner alternatively submits that the petitioner is inclined to pay an amount of Rs.80,000/- which may be given as compensation to PW.1.
11.

In the present circumstances, when the marriage has taken place in the year 1994 and thereafter the complaint was filed in the year 2007, further the petitioner has undergone nearly 14 years of trauma pending criminal case against him.

The petitioner is now aged more than 55 years and accordingly, this Court in the present circumstances is inclined to reduce the sentence of imprisonment to the period already undergone by the revision petitioner and to enhance the fine component.
The petitioner/accused No.1 shall pay an amount of Rs.81,000/- as fine before the trial Court, out of which, an amount of Rs.80,000/- shall be paid to PW.1 towards compensation.
In the event of failure by the petitioner to deposit the fine amount within four (04) weeks from the date of this Order, he shall undergo default sentence for six (06) months.
12. Accordingly, this Criminal Revision Case is allowed in-part.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.

K.SURENDER, J Date :15.07.2024 ynk Vanguri Veeraiah, vs The State Of Ap Rep By Its Pp Hyd., on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155801310/
